newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: China urged to play key role in Spratlys dispute.
newsitem.headline: China urged to play key role in Spratlys dispute.

text.p: China should take the initiative over joint development of the disputed Spratly Islands, an Asia-Pacific conference was told on Sunday.

"By taking the lead in putting joint development into action in spite of the difficulties involved, China's peaceful intention will be more credible," said Singapore Institute of International Affairs chairman Lee Lai To.
The Spratlys, a cluster of reefs and islets in the South China Sea believed to hold oil deposits, are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and the Philippines.

China, being the key player in the South China Sea disputes, is the major reference point in any confidence building attempt and since 1990 had been advocating joint development in the Spratlys, Lee said in a paper on maritime security cooperation presented at the Asia-Pacific Roundtable.
A high degree of political will was needed for the success of the joint scheme, he added.
He said that what were considered dangerous waters could be turned into an area of co-operation.
Lee said the initiation of joint development in the South China Sea would also forestall possible interference from outside powers and exploitation of the conflicts by others.
"It also demonstrates that Asian states could manage and sort out their own differences in their own way," he said.
